events.title: Anthropic set an IPO price range of $70 to $78 a share, which could raise up to about $64B at a valuation near $1.4 trillion, with trading expected around Nov 19.

events.who: Anthropic, TSMC, Nvidia, Google, Microsoft, AMD, Broadcom, Micron
events.title: TSMC joined Nvidia, Google, Microsoft, AMD, Broadcom and Micron in a $26B private placement of Anthropic stock that only completes if the IPO closes.
CoreWeave reports Q3 results with investors focused on its roughly $36B of debt, bond yields near 15.5% and how much more financing its backlog needs.
October consumer prices rose 0.4% on the month and core prices 0.3%, both above forecasts, lifting the odds of a Fed rate hike on Dec 9.
The Nasdaq fell after the hot October inflation report, ending the rebound that began the week, with Nvidia again among the weakest large stocks.
The Senate voted 73-25 to advance a permitting bill that would make data centers pay for their share of existing grid costs and for new lines and plants built for them.
SpaceX shares rose about 6% on Nov 9 as it advanced plans for a $24B data center and gas-fired power plant at Starbase in Texas.
CoreWeave is fighting a 'doom cycle' narrative as its debt costs and neocloud credit risk overshadow revenue growth.
Nvidia shares fell about 5% after the company opened an internal probe into CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with an alleged Chinese spy.
AMD jumped about 12% on an Oppenheimer upgrade and Broadcom gained 8% while Nvidia slid, lifting the chip index.
Mississippi regulators said SpaceXAI started building its Southaven data center without the required water discharge permits.
Musk said Tesla will end Cybertruck production and refund some deposits, shifting the factory capacity to Cybercab.
Microsoft sold $25B and Meta $15B of notes in early November as AI capex outran free cash flow at the largest tech firms.
Congress takes up a permitting bill with data center provisions, its first test on the issue after the midterm elections.
Jefferies raised its Eli Lilly price target to a Street-high $1,700, citing large overseas demand for its obesity drugs.
Banks and private credit funds are quietly stalling new AI data-center loans, with about $13.4B of data-center debt coming due in 2027.
Boeing plans to cut about 5% of its commercial aircraft workforce and slow its production ramp-up.
PJM's latest capacity auction cleared at a record $325 per megawatt-day yet fell short of its reliability target, with data centers blamed for nearly half of recent capacity costs.
ASML shares rose about 6% in a broad chip rally that excluded Nvidia.
A large Utah data center project faces rancher resistance over its use of historic water rights in a dry region.
October payrolls rose 165,000, well above forecasts, strengthening expectations of a Fed rate hike in December.
Anthropic's IPO valuation could be cut to around $1 trillion from a $1.5 trillion target, and the listing may be delayed after the AI stock rout, a report said.
The Nasdaq opened higher on Friday and recovered part of Thursday's AI sell-off, though tech stocks stayed below prior levels.
OpenAI reportedly closed about $11B as the first part of a scaled-back round valuing it at $1.25 trillion, below its earlier $1.4 trillion goal.
OpenAI's CFO said the company will keep building AI data centers despite midterm results that favored restrictions.

nvidia.news: Nvidia fell again on Nov 10 as the Nasdaq dropped after hot October inflation, following a 5% slide on Nov 9 over the board probe into CEO Jensen Huang and a 9% drop on Nov 5; rivals AMD, Broadcom and ASML rallied without it.
pros: Joins the $26B Anthropic placement tied to the IPO
Hyperscaler Q3 capex near $202B still flows mostly to its chips
cons: CEO probe and lawsuit raise leadership risk
Investors rotated to AMD, Broadcom and ASML
nvidia.weak: Leadership uncertainty arrives just as lenders pull back from funding its biggest debt-financed customers.

labs.news: Anthropic set an IPO range of $70-78 a share (Nov 10), up to about $64B raised at a valuation near $1.4T with trading expected Nov 19, plus a $26B chipmaker and Big Tech placement that depends on the IPO; OpenAI reportedly closed $11B at $1.25T (Nov 6).
pros: IPO range implies up to $1.4T, above last week's fears of $1T
Nvidia, Google, Microsoft, TSMC and others commit $26B alongside
cons: Anthropic lists about $900B of compute and lease commitments
A December Fed hike raises the discount rate on a loss-making listing
labs.weak: Both labs need public or private markets to stay open while the Fed is about to tighten.

bigtech.news: The Nasdaq fell on Nov 10 after October CPI came in hot, ending the Nov 9 rebound; Microsoft ($25B) and Meta ($15B) sold bonds in early November as Q3 capex near $202B outran cash flow, and BBB spreads are 1.13%, up 0.11 points in 30 days.

cloud.news: CoreWeave reports Q3 on Nov 10 with about $36B of debt, 2031 notes near 15.5% and default swaps above 1,150 bp, while the Senate advanced (73-25) a bill making data centers pay grid costs; HY spreads are 3.34%, up 0.23 points in 30 days, PJM demand is 3.9% above last year and Dallas and Taylor, TX remain 100% in drought.
pros: Bond yields eased from the 16.7% peak of Nov 5
CoreWeave says the election has not changed customer commitments
cons: Banks and private credit are stalling new data-center loans
Senate bill would shift grid costs onto data centers
cloud.weak: The backlog needs fresh financing just as lenders step back and yields sit in distressed territory.

citizens.news: October CPI rose 0.4% on the month (Nov 10); electricity CPI is up 5.4% y/y and energy CPI 21%, the saving rate is 3.8% and sentiment 48.1. PJM demand runs 3.9% and ERCOT 3.8% above last year (SRP in Phoenix is down 15%), PJM's capacity price hit a record $325/MW-day, and the Dallas and Taylor, TX hubs are 100% in drought.

spacex.news: SpaceX shares rose about 6% on Nov 9 on plans for a $24B data center and gas plant at Starbase, days after Mississippi regulators said its Southaven site was built without a water permit; ERCOT demand is up 3.8% y/y and gas is cheap at $2.63, but Texas hubs are fully in drought.

tesla.news: Musk said on Nov 9 that Tesla will end Cybertruck production and refund some deposits; the stock is still recovering from the post-midterm drop of Nov 4-5, and a December Fed hike would raise car-loan costs.

consumer.news: No major Apple news this week; imports from China are up 34% y/y and consumer sentiment is weak at 48.1 ahead of the holidays.

retail.news: Retail sales were up 6.3% y/y in September, but hot October CPI (Nov 10), a 3.8% saving rate and sentiment of 48.1 cloud the holiday season; e-commerce is 17.1% of sales.

autos.news: Light vehicle sales held at a 16.0M annual pace in October, flat y/y, with Ford's October sales slightly lower; a likely Fed hike on Dec 9 would push auto-loan rates up further.

fashion.news: Apparel prices are up 3.5% y/y (Oct) and imports from Vietnam are up 61%; no major fashion-brand news this week.

education.news: No notable news this week. Student loan balances near $1.78T keep pressure on young households as rates look set to rise.

banks.news: Banks and private credit funds are reported (Nov 9) to be stalling new AI data-center loans ahead of about $13.4B of data-center debt due in 2027; HY spreads are 3.34%, up 0.23 points in 30 days, and card delinquency is 2.85%.

fed.news: October CPI rose 0.4% and core 0.3% (Nov 10), both above forecasts, and markets now price a hike on Dec 9 as near certain, with Governor Waller floating a half point; fed funds is 3.88% in a 3.75-4.00% range, core PCE 3.1% vs the 2% goal, unemployment 4.1% and the 30-year mortgage 7.18%.
pros: 10-year yield is down 0.42 points over 30 days
cons: Core PCE at 3.1% and CPI re-accelerating
A hike lands on a credit market already stressed by AI debt
fed.weak: The Fed is set to tighten into the weakest AI credit conditions of the year.

chips.news: ASML rose about 6% and AMD about 12% on Nov 9 in a chip rally that left out Nvidia, and TSMC joined a $26B Anthropic stock placement (Nov 10); chip stocks slipped with the Nasdaq after the Nov 10 CPI report.

power.news: Power stocks such as Constellation and GE Vernova rebounded on Nov 9, PJM capacity cleared at a record $325/MW-day, and the Senate advanced a bill making data centers pay for new lines and plants; Henry Hub gas is $2.63.

healthco.news: Jefferies set a Street-high $1,700 target on Eli Lilly (Nov 9) after new obesity-pill trial data; medical care CPI is up a modest 1.9% y/y.

industrials.news: Boeing said on Nov 9 it will cut about 5% of its commercial aircraft workforce and slow its production ramp; slower data-center lending also clouds generator demand.

payments.news: No notable news this week. Consumer credit is up 3.0% y/y and card delinquency is 2.85%.

trade.news: The US-China truce was extended to Jan 10, 2027 and China signaled more US farm purchases (Nov 5); imports from China are up 34%, Mexico 40% and Vietnam 61% y/y, while customs duties are down 18%.
